chunks: Ibrahim ibn Hashim from more than one from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he asked him about the one who is unconscious for a month or forty nights, and he said.
He said, 'If you wish, I will inform you of what I command myself and my children to do: that you make up whatever missed you.'

key_terms.الْمَغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The one who is unconscious or in a coma
key_terms.فَاتَكَ: What missed you (i.e., what you missed due to incapacity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed prayers and fasting for someone who was unconscious for a long period?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *qada* (making up) for both prayers and fasting for one who is unconscious (*maghfa 'alayh*) for a month or forty nights. He grounds this ruling in his personal practice, stating that he commands himself and his offspring to fulfill these missed obligations, thereby highlighting the consistency between the Imam’s legal verdict and his own devotional conduct. This serves as a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for determining the duration and nature of missed acts of worship during prolonged unconsciousness.
